content_of_post_to_comment:
I was talking to a friend recently… he’s 34, been single his entire life, decent career, financially stable, takes care of himself. No addictions, no drama. Honestly, from the outside you’d probably think he’s doing just fine. Then he said something that stayed with me. He said, well… maybe some people are just not meant to find someone. That honestly caught me off guard.

He’s been on dates over the years. Some went nowhere. A few women picked expensive restaurants and they seemed to be interested… until the bill was paid and then people slowly disappeared …. He’s not even angry about it anymore. He just expects it now. He told me the hardest part isn’t getting rejected. It’s slowly starting to believe that nobody is ever going to choose you.

He still goes to work every day. People think he has everything together. They joke with him, ask about work, ask about investments, ask about travel. Nobody asks him what it feels like to spend every birthday, every holiday, every weekend… wondering if this is simply how the rest of life is going to look.

He said sometimes he sees couples arguing in public and still thinks, I would probably trade places with them just to know what it feels like to matter to someone. Then he laughed for a second and said, I… I don’t even know what I would talk about if I actually met someone now. That part aactually hit me!!

It feels like after enough years alone, it stops being only about dating. It starts changing how you see yourself. am thinking …. if this is becoming more common than people realize. For the men here, especially those in their thirties who’ve built a stable career… does any of this sound familiar.

And for the women reading this, have you met men who seemed successful on the surface but were quietly carrying something like this. I’d really like to hear different perspectives because I honestly don’t know if my friend is an exception, or if there are far more people feeling this than anyone talks about.
comment: The line about not knowing what he’d talk about if he met someone now feels very real. Long periods alone can make people rusty at being vulnerable, not because they have nothing to offer, but because they stop practicing that part of themselves. I wonder how many people mistake being out of practice for being incapable of connection.
